scope: Pinned official MCP client SDK 2.3.1 modern stdio transport generates overload requests against a local debug server in a route-free Linux namespace with controlled HTTP/DNS fixtures. This is not a package-installed or official-candidate test.
reproduce: npm ci --prefix tools/mcp-sdk-probe --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund && OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR="$PWD/tools/mcp-sdk-probe" bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp

fixture.network: disposable namespace, no external route; allowed.test resolves to 11.0.0.1 on namespace loopback
fixture.client_generated_sequence: held /cancel-drip GET; eight 60000-byte tools/list requests; ninth marked guarded_fetch; SDK AbortSignal cancellation; audit read; approved /plain GET
expected_and_observed: ninth request rejected with protocol code -32000 and MCP_INPUT_BUSY
held fetch cancelled and EGRESS_CANCELLED audited
cancelled fixture socket closed while client remained live
HTTP hits exactly /cancel-drip and /plain; no marked busy URL hit
same-process recovery GET returned EGRESS_ALLOWED and fixture-ok

full_suite_result: 2259 MCP decisions reported by the run; all assertions passed
cleanup: Probe wrapper removed its namespace and resolver directory; no outbound-guard-probe namespace remained after exit.
limitations: One finite client-originated burst with an SDK control API, not a desktop or terminal UI. This does not show Claude Code, Codex or Cursor generating these overload frames; the package-installed native-client saturation fixture still uses a bridge. No resource peak was sampled during the 0.05-second burst, no arbitrary concurrency or traffic from other tools is covered, and this is not exact official-candidate qualification.
